pathways.title: Pathway 1: A.A. in Accounting (Transfer / CPA Track)

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Accounting
steps.description: Complete foundational university transfer coursework in accounting, economics, and business administration at Miami Dade College.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University
steps.description: Transfer to an accredited university such as FIU, UF, or UCF with upper-division standing under Florida's 2+2 articulation agreement.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Complete advanced coursework in financial auditing, cost accounting, corporate taxation, and accounting information systems.

steps.name: Accounting Internship or Supervised Experience
steps.description: Gain mandatory professional work experience in public accounting, corporate finance, or government auditing under the direct supervision of a licensed CPA.

steps.name: Uniform CPA Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Complete 120 semester hours of college education including upper-level accounting coursework, register with the Florida Board of Accountancy, pass all four sections of the computer-based Uniform CPA Exam, and complete 150 total semester hours for full CPA licensure.

steps.name: Master of Science in Accounting
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Complete a graduate degree in accounting or taxation to satisfy the 150 credit hour CPA licensure requirement and qualify for specialized accounting roles.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: A.S. in Accounting Technology (Applied Technical Track)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Accounting Technology
steps.description: Develop immediate, practical skills in computerized accounting software, payroll systems, tax preparation, and general ledger reconciliation.

steps.name: Accounting Assistant / Bookkeeper Internship
steps.description: Acquire hands-on corporate finance experience assisting with accounts payable, accounts receivable, and financial statement preparation.

steps.name: Articulation to Bachelor's Degree Program
steps.description: Transfer A.S. credits into a baccalaureate program such as a Bachelor of Applied Science (B.A.S.) or articulated B.S. in Accounting degree.

steps.name: Bachelor of Applied Science or Bachelor of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Complete upper-division coursework in business law, managerial accounting, and corporate governance to broaden employment eligibility.

steps.name: Certified Management Accountant (CMA) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution, complete two years of continuous professional experience in financial management, and pass the two-part CMA examination.

steps.name: Master of Business Administration (MBA)
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Pursue an MBA or Master's degree in Finance to qualify for executive leadership positions such as Financial Controller or CFO.

requirements: Check the official certification website for specific education prerequisites
Complete required coursework or training program
Apply for examination with the certifying organization
Pass the required examination(s)
Meet state-specific or jurisdiction-specific requirements
Active membership in the Institute of Management Accountants (IMA)
A bachelor's degree from an accredited college/university or an approved professional certification
Two continuous years of professional experience in management accounting or financial management
Pass Part 1 (Financial Planning, Performance, and Analytics) and Part 2 (Strategic Financial Management) of the CMA Exam
Comply with the IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice

pathways.title: Pathway 1: A.A. in Engineering - Mechanical

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Mechanical
steps.description: Complete foundational lower-division coursework in calculus, physics, and basic engineering mechanics at Miami Dade College to build the groundwork for aerospace systems.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Aerospace Program
steps.description: Transfer to an accredited university (e.g., FIU, UF, UCF) offering an ABET-accredited Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering under Florida transfer articulation agreements.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: Complete upper-division coursework in aerodynamics, propulsion, orbital mechanics, aerospace structures, and flight dynamics.

steps.name: Aerospace Engineering Internship or Co-op
steps.description: Gain practical industry experience through supervised internships with aerospace manufacturers, defense contractors, or space agencies like NASA.

steps.name: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Complete an ABET-accredited engineering degree or be in final year of study; Register with NCEES; Pass the 6-hour computer-based FE exam covering core engineering concepts.

steps.name: Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Pass the FE exam; Complete 4 years of progressive engineering experience under a licensed PE; Pass the PE exam in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering for state licensure.

steps.name: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Pursue advanced graduate study to specialize in fields such as hypersonics, satellite propulsion, or autonomous flight systems.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: A.A. in Engineering - Electrical

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Electrical
steps.description: Complete core lower-division math, physics, and circuit design coursework at Miami Dade College, ideal for students focusing on avionics and spacecraft electrical systems.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Engineering Program
steps.description: Transfer to a university offering a Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering with an emphasis on avionics, control systems, and signal processing.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: Earn a bachelor's degree focusing on flight controls, avionics systems, satellite navigation, and electromagnetic interference in aircraft.

steps.name: Avionics and Flight Systems Internship
steps.description: Complete hands-on internships working on guidance, navigation, and aerospace electronics under the mentorship of senior engineers.

steps.name: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from an ABET-accredited bachelor's program; Apply through NCEES; Pass the computer-based 6-hour FE exam.

steps.name: Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Hold FE certification; Document 4 years of verified engineering practice supervised by a licensed engineer; Pass the official PE exam.

steps.name: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Obtain a master's degree to lead high-level research and development projects in satellite communications and avionics integration.

requirements: Possess an EAC/ABET-accredited bachelor's degree in engineering, or be an undergraduate student nearing completion of an accredited program (varies by state licensing board)
Create a MyNCEES account and select your designated state/territorial licensing board
Obtain state licensing board approval prior to registering, if required by your specific board
Register for the exam through MyNCEES and pay the standard $225 exam registration fee
Schedule and pass the 5-hour 20-minute computer-based exam consisting of 110 questions in your chosen engineering discipline
Earn a bachelor's degree in engineering from an ABET-accredited program (or board-approved equivalent)
Pass the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
Gain required progressive engineering work experience under a licensed Professional Engineer (typically 4 years, depending on the state board)
Submit an application and receive approval from your specific state licensing board
Create an NCEES account to register for and schedule the CBT exam

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Science in Aviation Administration

steps.name: Associate in Science in Aviation Administration
steps.description: Earn an Associate in Science degree at Miami Dade College covering aviation fundamentals, airspace systems, airport management, and aviation safety.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Aviation CTI Program
steps.description: Transfer credits to a four-year institution offering an FAA Collegiate Training Initiative (CTI) or accredited aviation program, such as Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University or Florida Institute of Technology.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aviation Management
steps.description: Complete a bachelor's degree focused on airspace systems, air traffic management, and regulations to maximize competitiveness for FAA hiring bids.

steps.name: FAA Air Traffic Skills Assessment (ATSA) & FAA Academy Training
steps.description: Requirements: U.S. citizenship, under age 31 at application deadline, pass medical and security background clearances, pass the computer-based ATSA exam, and successfully graduate from the FAA Academy in Oklahoma City.

steps.name: FAA Air Traffic Control Facility On-the-Job Training
steps.description: Complete intensive, supervised on-the-job training (OJT) at an assigned air traffic control tower, terminal radar approach control (TRACON), or en-route center facility.

steps.name: Certified Tower Operator (CTO) & Specialist Certification
steps.description: Requirements: Pass practical tests and facility checkout evaluations to earn the FAA Air Traffic Control Specialist credential and facility-specific certifications.

steps.name: Master of Science in Aviation Safety or Management (Optional)
steps.description: Pursue an optional graduate degree in aviation safety or management for advancement into executive leadership and supervisory roles within the FAA.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Science in Professional Pilot Technology

steps.name: Associate in Science in Professional Pilot Technology
steps.description: Build comprehensive knowledge of flight operations, airspace navigation, meteorology, and radio communications through MDC's pilot program.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Aviation Program
steps.description: Transfer your MDC associate degree toward a bachelor's degree in aviation science or technology at an accredited university.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Science
steps.description: Earn a bachelor's degree in aeronautical science or flight technology to fulfill educational prerequisites for FAA public hiring tracks.

steps.name: FAA Air Traffic Skills Assessment (ATSA) & FAA Academy Training
steps.description: Requirements: U.S. citizenship, under age 31, pass Class 1 FAA medical exam, clear security background check, achieve competitive ATSA exam score, and pass FAA Academy training.

steps.name: Supervised Air Traffic Facility On-the-Job Training
steps.description: Undergo facility-specific practical training under the direct supervision of veteran air traffic controllers.

steps.name: Certified Tower Operator (CTO) / Radar Certification
steps.description: Requirements: Complete local position certifications and pass oral and practical exams administered by FAA evaluators to achieve full controller status.

requirements: Be a United States citizen
Be under 31 years of age prior to the closing date of the vacancy announcement (exceptions apply for eligible military veterans or candidates with prior ATC experience)

Have 3 years of progressively responsible work experience, OR a 4-year Bachelor's degree, OR a combination of post-secondary education and work experience totaling 3 years (or graduate from an FAA Air Traffic-Collegiate Training Initiative (AT-CTI) program)
Achieve a qualifying score on the FAA Air Traffic Skills Assessment (ATSA)
Pass a medical examination, drug screening, and background security clearance
Speak English clearly enough to be understood over radio and communications equipment
Successfully complete initial training at the FAA Academy in Oklahoma City after receiving a Conditional Employment Offer (CEO)
Must be at least 18 years of age
Must hold at least a valid FAA Second-Class Airman Medical Certificate issued under 14 CFR Part 67
Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand the English language fluently without impediment to radio communications
Must pass the FAA Control Tower Operator written knowledge examination covering air traffic control procedures, meteorology, and radio navigation
Must pass a practical test demonstrating knowledge and skill in performing tower duties and obtain a facility rating at an operational air traffic control tower
Must be at least 18 years of age
Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand the English language fluently
Must hold a valid FAA Second-Class Medical Certificate issued under 14 CFR Part 67
Must pass the FAA Control Tower Operator (CTO) written knowledge examination
Must complete facility-specific training and demonstrate competency at an operational air traffic control tower
Must pass a practical test (facility rating) administered by an authorized FAA examiner or designated facility evaluator under 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart B

pathways.title: Pathway 1: A.S. in Aviation Maintenance Management

steps.name: Associate in Science in Aviation Maintenance Management
steps.description: Provides comprehensive technical instruction in aircraft structures, systems, powerplants, and maintenance regulations required for an aviation maintenance career.

steps.name: Aviation Maintenance Practical Training
steps.description: Gain hands-on maintenance experience working on real aircraft systems under direct supervision of FAA-licensed mechanics.

steps.name: FAA Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) Certificate
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from an FAA-certificated maintenance school or complete required practical work experience; Pass FAA Written Knowledge Tests (General, Airframe, Powerplant); Pass Oral and Practical Exams administered by an FAA Designated Mechanic Examiner (DME).

steps.name: Transfer to 4-Year University
steps.description: Optional transfer path to upper-division programs at institutions such as Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University or Florida International University for career advancement.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Maintenance Management or Aeronautics
steps.description: Optional bachelor's degree focused on leadership, safety compliance, and operational management in commercial or corporate aviation.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: A.S. in Aviation Administration

steps.name: Associate in Science in Aviation Administration
steps.description: Focuses on aviation management, logistics, regulations, and business practices for students seeking a broader entry into aviation operations alongside technical training.

steps.name: On-the-Job Aircraft Maintenance Apprenticeship
steps.description: Obtain 18 to 30 months of practical hands-on experience under certified mechanics to meet FAA experience requirements for certification.

steps.name: FAA Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) Certificate
steps.description: Requirements: Document required months of supervised maintenance experience; Pass FAA General, Airframe, and Powerplant written examinations; Successfully pass FAA Oral and Practical testing.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aviation Management
steps.description: Prepares experienced technicians for leadership roles such as Quality Assurance Director, Maintenance Supervisor, or Chief Inspector.

requirements: Be at least 18 years old
Be able to read, write, speak, and understand the English language

Graduate from an FAA-certificated Aviation Maintenance Technician School (14 CFR Part 147) OR complete at least 18 months of practical experience for a single rating (Airframe or Powerplant), or 30 months of combined experience for both ratings
Present proof of experience or graduation to an FAA inspector to receive approval and signed FAA Form 8610-2 (Airman Certificate and/or Rating Application)
Pass three computer-based written knowledge tests (General, Airframe, and Powerplant) with a score of 70% or higher
Pass an Oral and Practical (O&P) test administered by a Designated Mechanic Examiner (DME)

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Science in Animation & Game Art (Technical Focus)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Animation & Game Art
steps.description: Gain hands-on technical skills in 2D and 3D animation, character design, storyboarding, and digital art tools at Miami Dade College.

steps.name: Transfer to University Animation Program
steps.description: Transfer credits to a four-year institution (such as UCF, FIU, or specialized art institutes) to complete a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree. Admission typically requires maintaining a minimum 2.5 GPA and submitting a portfolio.

steps.name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Animation
steps.description: Complete advanced visual effects, character rigging, and production pipeline training to finalize a professional demo reel.

steps.name: Animation Studio Internship
steps.description: Gain practical experience in a production studio working under senior animators to develop studio-ready assets and pipeline expertise.

steps.name: Autodesk Certified Professional in Maya
steps.description: Requirements: Complete official Maya training or equivalent industry experience, pass the 120-minute computer-based practical exam, and demonstrate proficiency in 3D modeling, animation, and rendering tools.

steps.name: Master of Fine Arts in Animation
steps.description: An optional graduate degree focused on creative directing, advanced visual storytelling, or post-secondary teaching in digital arts.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Arts in Computer Arts Animation (Transfer Focus)

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Computer Arts Animation
steps.description: Build foundational artistic principles, drawing skills, and general education prerequisites designed for seamless transfer into a four-year university visual arts program.

steps.name: Transfer to a University Fine Arts Program
steps.description: Utilize Florida statewide articulation agreements to transfer into a B.F.A. or B.A. program in Animation or Media Arts at a state university or art academy.

steps.name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Digital Arts and Animation
steps.description: Develop high-level digital animation techniques, visual story development, and collaborative film or game production projects.

steps.name: Production Apprenticeship / Portfolio Practicum
steps.description: Participate in real-world studio apprenticeships or capstone portfolio reviews with industry professionals to prepare for job placement.

steps.name: Adobe Certified Professional in Digital Video / Motion Graphics
steps.description: Requirements: Complete coursework or relevant experience in After Effects and Premiere Pro, and pass the Adobe Certified Professional performance-based examination.

steps.name: Master of Fine Arts in Digital Media
steps.description: An optional master's program for those seeking senior art director positions, studio leadership, or academic faculty positions.

pathways.title: Pathway 3: Associate in Science in Game Development & Design (Game Animation Focus)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Game Development & Design
steps.description: Focus on interactive character movement, game engine integration, and technical asset creation for interactive media at Miami Dade College.

steps.name: Transfer to Interactive Entertainment / Game Art Program
steps.description: Transfer to a university specialization program in Game Art or Interactive Entertainment to refine real-time animation skills.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Game Art and Animation
steps.description: Study motion capture, real-time physics animation, state machines, and environmental art within interactive graphics pipelines.

steps.name: Game Studio Internship
steps.description: Work directly with game developers, riggers, and programmers to implement animated assets into interactive game engines.

steps.name: Unreal Engine / Unity Certified Associate
steps.description: Requirements: Knowledge of modern game engine workflows, completion of practical technical tests, and passing the official engine certification exam.

steps.name: Master of Science in Interactive Entertainment
steps.description: An optional advanced degree for specializing in technical art direction, procedural animation, or game studio management.

requirements: Recommended 400 to 1,200 hours of hands-on, real-world experience using Autodesk Maya
Demonstrated proficiency in key Maya workflows including modeling, rigging, animation, dynamics, lighting, and rendering
Completion of advanced Autodesk Maya training coursework or equivalent professional industry experience
Create an Autodesk account and register for the exam through the Autodesk Certification portal
Pass the Autodesk Certified Professional in Maya exam, which consists of multiple-choice and interactive, performance-based questions within the allotted time
Pass the 'Visual Effects & Motion Graphics using Adobe After Effects' exam
Pass the 'Digital Video using Adobe Premiere Pro' exam to earn the 'Adobe Certified Professional in Digital Video' specialty credential
Recommended minimum of 150 hours of instruction and hands-on experience with Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects software
Create a Certiport user account and purchase an exam voucher or register through an authorized testing center
Achieve a passing score on the 50-minute live-in-the-application exam
Recommended 150 to 200 hours of hands-on training and experience with Unity software
Create an official Unity account to manage certification credentials
Register for the exam through an authorized testing partner (such as Certiport or Pearson VUE)
Purchase an official exam voucher or register through an accredited educational institution
Pass the Unity Certified Associate exam (a proctored exam featuring multiple-choice and practical scenario questions)

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Arts in Architecture (Recommended Transfer Track)

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Architecture
steps.description: Completes lower-division general education and foundational architectural design studio courses required to transfer into a professional university program.

steps.name: Transfer to a NAAB-Accredited Architecture Program
steps.description: Transfer to a four-year institution such as FIU, UF, or FAU via Florida articulation agreements, requiring a competitive GPA and design portfolio submission.

steps.name: Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) or Bachelor of Science in Architecture
steps.description: Complete a 5-year professional B.Arch degree or a 4-year B.S. in Architecture, mastering architectural history, theory, building systems, and advanced design.

steps.name: Architectural Experience Program (AXP)
steps.description: Complete 3,740 required hours of structured professional experience under the direct supervision of a licensed architect across six practice areas.

steps.name: Architect Registration Examination (A.R.E.)
steps.description: Requirements: NAAB-accredited degree or state board authorization, Active participation/completion of AXP requirements, Pass all 6 divisions of the A.R.E. (Practice Management, Project Management, Programming & Analysis, Project Planning & Design, Project Development & Documentation, and Construction & Evaluation).

steps.name: Master of Architecture (M.Arch)
steps.description: Optional post-professional or professional degree for students seeking advanced specialization, academic teaching credentials, or firm leadership.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Architectural

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Architectural
steps.description: Provides foundational math, science, and lower-division engineering/architecture coursework for students interested in technical and structural architectural engineering paths.

steps.name: Transfer to University Architecture/Engineering Program
steps.description: Transfer into a professional bachelor's program at an accredited university subject to prerequisite completion and portfolio evaluation.

steps.name: Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) or Bachelor of Science in Architectural Engineering
steps.description: Earn a bachelor's degree focusing on building technology, structural engineering, environmental controls, and architectural design.

steps.name: Architectural Experience Program (AXP)
steps.description: Accumulate 3,740 hours of practical experience supervised by a licensed architect or professional engineer in accordance with NCARB standards.

steps.name: Architect Registration Examination (A.R.E.)
steps.description: Requirements: Recognized architectural degree, Completion of required AXP hours, Registration with state board, Pass all 6 divisions of the A.R.E.

steps.name: Master of Architecture (M.Arch)
steps.description: Optional advanced graduate degree for structural architectural specialists seeking higher technical expertise or teaching roles.

pathways.title: Pathway 3: Associate in Science in Architectural Design and Construction Technology

steps.name: Associate in Science in Architectural Design and Construction Technology
steps.description: Focuses on practical computer-aided drafting (CAD), Building Information Modeling (BIM), building materials, codes, and construction management.

steps.name: Transfer to NAAB-Accredited B.Arch / M.Arch Program
steps.description: Transfer technical credits into a university architecture program, often requiring supplemental general education and studio courses.

steps.name: Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) or Bachelor of Science in Architectural Studies
steps.description: Complete upper-division degree requirements necessary to satisfy educational prerequisites for state architectural licensure.

steps.name: Architectural Experience Program (AXP)
steps.description: Complete 3,740 hours of supervised, real-world architectural design and project management experience.

steps.name: Architect Registration Examination (A.R.E.)
steps.description: Requirements: Educational qualification verified by state board, Full AXP completion, Pass all six computer-based A.R.E. division exams.

steps.name: Master of Architecture (M.Arch)
steps.description: Optional Master's degree to fulfill NAAB accreditation requirements if the bachelor's degree was non-NAAB accredited.

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Biomedical (Transfer Route)

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Biomedical
steps.description: Complete lower-division coursework in calculus, physics, chemistry, and introductory engineering concepts designed to seamlessly transfer into a university biomedical engineering program.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University
steps.description: Transfer to an ABET-accredited university, such as Florida International University (FIU) or University of Florida (UF), maintaining a competitive GPA for major admission.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
steps.description: Complete upper-division specialized coursework in biomaterials, biomechanics, tissue engineering, and medical instrumentation, including a senior capstone design project.

steps.name: Biomedical Engineering Internship / Co-Op
steps.description: Gain relevant professional experience in medical device manufacturing, biotechnology research labs, or clinical healthcare environments under professional supervision.

steps.name: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Complete an ABET-accredited bachelor's degree in engineering, Register with NCEES, Pass the 6-hour computer-based FE exam to obtain Engineer Intern (EI) designation.

steps.name: Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Hold an active FE certification, Complete at least 4 years of qualifying engineering experience under a licensed PE, Pass the PE exam for professional licensure.

steps.name: Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Pursue an advanced graduate degree for specialized research and development positions, advanced industry roles, or academic teaching.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Science in Biomedical Engineering Technology (Technical & Applied Route)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Biomedical Engineering Technology
steps.description: Gain hands-on practical skills in inspecting, calibrating, maintaining, and repairing complex medical equipment used in hospitals and clinical settings.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University
steps.description: Transfer to a four-year institution offering a Bachelor of Science in Engineering Technology or Biomedical Engineering to expand technical and engineering theoretical background.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering Technology / Engineering
steps.description: Complete upper-division coursework in advanced systems analysis, clinical engineering management, and medical device design.

steps.name: Clinical Engineering Internship
steps.description: Participate in structured clinical rotations maintaining diagnostic and therapeutic medical devices alongside certified biomedical technicians and engineers.

steps.name: Certified Biomedical Equipment Technician (CBET)
steps.description: Requirements: Complete an associate degree in biomedical equipment technology, Accumulate required full-time work experience, Pass the CBET certification exam by AAMI.

steps.name: Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Pursue a master's degree to shift focus into advanced medical device research, product design, or clinical systems engineering.

requirements: Meet one of the following eligibility pathways: 1) Associate degree in biomedical equipment technology plus 2 years of full-time BMET work experience; 2) Associate degree in electronics technology plus 3 years of full-time BMET work experience; or 3) 4 years of full-time BMET work experience.
Submit a completed online application along with candidate documentation and the required exam fee to the AAMI Credentials Institute (ACI).
Pass the CBET examination, which consists of 165 multiple-choice questions to be completed within a 3-hour time limit.

Candidate-in-Training status option: Candidates who meet the educational requirements but lack the necessary work experience may take the exam and earn candidate-in-training status, with 5 years to fulfill the work experience requirement.

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Science in Nursing (Direct RN to BSN Track)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Nursing
steps.description: Earn your Associate degree to gain fundamental nursing knowledge and become eligible to sit for the registered nursing licensure exam.

steps.name: NCLEX-RN Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from an accredited nursing program, Apply to state board of nursing, Receive Authorization to Test (ATT), Pass the NCLEX-RN computer-adaptive exam.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Nursing
steps.description: Complete MDC's RN-to-BSN program to build advanced leadership and public health skills necessary for graduate admissions.

steps.name: Labor & Delivery RN Experience
steps.description: Gain 1-2 years of clinical registered nursing experience in labor and delivery, postpartum, or women's health units.

steps.name: Master of Science in Nursing - Nurse-Midwifery
steps.description: Complete an ACME-accredited graduate nurse-midwifery program providing didactic and clinical training in antepartum, intrapartum, and gynecological care.

steps.name: AMCB Midwifery Certification Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from an ACME-accredited nurse-midwifery program, Hold active unencumbered RN license, Pass the 4-hour AMCB national certification exam.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Arts in Pre-Nursing (Transfer Track)

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Pre-Nursing
steps.description: Complete general education prerequisites and core science requirements required for entry into a university bachelor's nursing program.

steps.name: Transfer to University B.S.N. Program
steps.description: Transfer seamlessly to a university such as FIU, UF, or UCF under Florida articulation agreements with a competitive GPA.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Nursing
steps.description: Complete a 2-year traditional upper-division BSN program covering comprehensive clinical rotations and advanced nursing science.

steps.name: NCLEX-RN Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from accredited BSN program, Submit background check and board application, Receive ATT, Pass the NCLEX-RN exam.

steps.name: Obstetric Clinical Experience
steps.description: Work as a licensed RN in acute obstetrics or maternal-child nursing to satisfy entry requirements for graduate midwifery programs.

steps.name: Master of Science in Nursing - Nurse-Midwifery
steps.description: Enrol in a specialized master's program focusing on comprehensive primary healthcare for women and infant care.

steps.name: AMCB Midwifery Certification Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Complete accredited Nurse-Midwifery degree, Maintain current active RN license, Pass the national AMCB certification exam for APRN licensure.

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Arts (A.A.) in Accounting Transfer Route

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Accounting
steps.description: Complete foundational general education and lower-division business prerequisites at MDC to prepare for smooth transfer into a university accounting program.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University
steps.description: Transfer to an accredited university such as Florida International University (FIU) or University of Florida (UF) under Florida's statewide articulation agreement.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Complete upper-division coursework in financial accounting, auditing, corporate taxation, cost accounting, and business law.

steps.name: Master of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Fulfill Florida's 150 total semester credit hour requirement for CPA licensure through specialized graduate coursework in accounting and taxation.

steps.name: Supervised Accounting Experience
steps.description: Complete at least one year (2,000 hours) of professional accounting experience under the direct supervision of a licensed CPA.

steps.name: Uniform Certified Public Accountant (CPA) Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Complete at least 120 credit hours to sit for the exam (150 hours for licensure), pass all four sections of the Uniform CPA Exam (AUD, FAR, REG, and a Discipline section), and complete the Florida Board of Accountancy ethics exam.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Science (A.S.) in Accounting Technology Technical Route

steps.name: Associate in Science in Accounting Technology
steps.description: Gain technical hands-on experience in payroll, tax preparation, accounting software, and financial recordkeeping for immediate workplace entry and workforce advancement.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Program
steps.description: Transfer articulated credits into a Bachelor of Applied Science or Bachelor of Science degree program at a participating four-year institution.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Complete advanced coursework in auditing, advanced financial accounting, business law, and managerial reporting to satisfy CPA exam course distribution requirements.

steps.name: Supervised Professional Experience
steps.description: Obtain one year of full-time work experience performing accounting duties under a licensed Certified Public Accountant.

steps.name: Uniform Certified Public Accountant (CPA) Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Complete 150 total semester hours including 30 upper-level accounting credits and 24 business credits, pass all four parts of the computer-based Uniform CPA Exam, and apply for state licensure.

steps.name: Master of Accounting / Master of Taxation
steps.description: Optionally pursue a specialized master's degree in taxation or forensic accounting to enhance career advancement opportunities in public or corporate accounting.

pathways.title: Pathway 1: Associate in Science in Nursing (Direct Clinical Track)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Nursing - R.N.
steps.description: Complete hands-on clinical coursework and practical training required to become a registered nurse.

steps.name: NCLEX-RN Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from an accredited nursing program, Apply for licensure with the Florida Board of Nursing, Receive Authorization to Test (ATT), Pass the NCLEX-RN exam.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Nursing
steps.description: Complete MDC's RN-to-BSN program to build advanced skills in leadership, research, and evidence-based practice necessary for graduate study.

steps.name: Critical Care Clinical Experience
steps.description: Obtain a minimum of 1-2 years of full-time professional nursing experience in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU) or critical care setting.

steps.name: Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) in Nurse Anesthesia
steps.description: Complete an accredited doctoral program in nurse anesthesia covering advanced pharmacology, physiology, and clinical anesthesia residency.

steps.name: National Certification Examination (NCE)

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Arts in Pre-Nursing (University Transfer Track)

requirements: Check the official certification website for specific education prerequisites
Complete required coursework or training program
Apply for examination with the certifying organization
Pass the required examination(s)
Meet state-specific or jurisdiction-specific requirements
Be a United States citizen
Be under 31 years of age prior to the closing date of the application period (with limited exceptions for individuals with prior military/ATC experience)
Have a 4-year bachelor's degree, 3 years of progressively responsible full-time work experience, or an equivalent combination of post-secondary education and work experience
Pass the Air Traffic Skills Assessment (AT-SA) exam
Pass a medical examination, security background check, and substance screen
Speak English clearly enough to be understood over communications equipment
Complete training at the FAA Academy in Oklahoma City upon selection

requirements: Be at least 18 years old
Be able to read, write, speak, and understand the English language

Graduate from an FAA-certificated Aviation Maintenance Technician School (Part 147) OR document at least 18 months of practical experience for one rating (Airframe or Powerplant) or 30 months of concurrent experience for both ratings
Obtain FAA authorization to test by submitting FAA Form 8610-2 and interviewing with an inspector at a local FAA Flight Standards District Office (FSDO)
Pass the required FAA Knowledge (written) tests: General, Airframe, and/or Powerplant
Pass an Oral and Practical (O&P) exam for the desired rating(s) administered by a Designated Mechanic Examiner (DME)
No formal educational prerequisites or prior work experience required to take the core AET examination
Create an candidate account through ASTM International and register for the examination
Pay the standard examination fee (typically $175)
Pass the 80-question multiple-choice computer-based examination with a minimum score of 70%
Maintain certification by completing recertification requirements or retaking the exam every 5 years

requirements: Establish and maintain an active NCARB Record
Meet the educational requirement of your chosen jurisdiction (typically a professional degree in architecture from an NAAB-accredited program)
Request and obtain eligibility to test from a state/jurisdictional architectural licensing board
Enroll in or complete the Architectural Experience Program (AXP), which requires earning a minimum of 3,740 hours across six practice areas
Pass all six divisions of ARE 5.0 (Practice Management, Project Management, Programming & Analysis, Project Planning & Design, Project Development & Documentation, and Construction & Evaluation)

Submit an official online application through PMI detailing project experience and education hours for audit and approval.
Pass the official proctored exam (150 questions for CAPM; 180 questions for PMP).
Secondary degree (high school diploma, associate's degree, or global equivalent)
21 contact hours of formal training in agile practices
12 months of general project experience within the last 5 years (an active PMP® or PgMP® satisfies this requirement)
8 months of agile project experience within the last 3 years (earned in addition to general project experience)
Submit an online application through PMI and pass the 120-question PMI-ACP examination

requirements: No prior formal education or specific work experience prerequisites required
Complete and submit the official AWS Certified Welder Application form
Pass a practical hands-on welding performance test at an AWS Accredited Test Facility (ATF) following a specific Welding Procedure Specification (WPS)
Have the practical welding performance test inspected and verified by an AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI)
Maintain certification by submitting a Certification Maintenance Application every six months to verify continuous welding employment
